industry.headline: Google, TikTok and Meta Sue California Over New Social Media Law
industry.summary: Google, TikTok and Meta filed a federal suit to block a new California law limiting addictive design features for under-16s, days after Meta settled a landmark New Mexico suit over misleading platform-safety claims. Keeps regulatory uncertainty high in NOMO's core US GTM market while reinforcing the 'addictive feeds are a recognized harm' narrative that supports NOMO's off-social-media rewards positioning with schools.

industry.headline: UK Weighs Expanding Under-16 Social Media Ban to YouTube Kids, Spotify and Lego Play Over Recommenders
industry.summary: UK ministers are now considering a catch-all expansion of the under-16 ban to any recommender-driven, user-generated-content service (potentially 150 sites) by March, walking back earlier promised exemptions, with a parliamentary bill due in December. A fast-moving shift in NOMO's UK pilot market where CEO Leonardo is actively engaged on policy, potentially redefining what counts as 'off-platform' behavior NOMO rewards.

industry.headline: Meta's AI Age-Check Goes Global: Can It Protect Teens?
industry.summary: Meta is rolling out AI-based age checks globally as more countries (UK, Indonesia, Australia, Turkiye) weigh under-age social media bans, but Australia's experience shows enforcement is leaky — eSafety found over 80% of preteens/young teens still using social media six months after the ban despite hundreds of thousands of account takedowns. Strengthens the case for incentive-based complements like NOMO alongside prohibition-only approaches, relevant to UK and AU signal.

reconsider.name: AppBlock
reconsider.reason: Generic, weakly sourced listicle mention; not distinctive enough versus stronger competitor candidates kept.
reconsider.why_fits: AppBlock is a maturing app-blocking tool with strict schedule/location-based profiles and a 'turns focus time into a small game' positioning, squarely matching the explicit 'app block' competitor criteria.

reconsider.name: Lock&Stock
reconsider.reason: Weak region fit (UAE/Pakistan, not a priority market); redundant with The Commons App's school-focused niche.
reconsider.why_fits: <cite index="4-1,4-2">Lock&Stock is a free mobile app for students that allows them to earn keys each time their phones are locked, with longer lock time earning more rewards.</cite> It directly competes for in-school phone-reduction rewards programs and EdTech procurement, overlapping with NOMO's school channel strategy, though currently concentrated in UAE/Pakistan markets.

reconsider.name: LockedIn
reconsider.reason: Redundant with The Commons App in the same school phone-lock enforcement niche; medium confidence with no distinguishing specifics.
reconsider.why_fits: LockedIn builds software that locks student phones on campus during school hours to help districts comply with new phone-free laws, directly competing with NOMO for school/district EdTech contracts as more states mandate phone-free policies.

reconsider.name: Guggenheim Museum Teen Circle / ICA Boston Teen Programs
reconsider.reason: Overlaps with TDF Tickets for Teens and existing Fever partnership; medium confidence.
reconsider.why_fits: Unlike a generic ticketing aggregator, these are teen-specific (ages 13-18) museum membership programs offering exclusive events, advance ticket access, and peer-led experiences built just for Gen Z — a distinct, realistic-to-deal-with inventory type (exclusive teen access rather than generic tickets) that fills a gap next to NOMO's existing Fever/museum-ticket partnership.

reconsider.name: Guggenheim Teen Circle / GuggTeens
reconsider.reason: Overlaps with Carnegie's broader reciprocal teen-membership offer; redundant single-city museum perk.
reconsider.why_fits: The Guggenheim's free Teen Circle membership for ages 13-18 provides access to exclusive events, performances, and group activities for members and their friends, which is tradeable, teen-specific reward inventory not currently covered by NOMO's museum/event partners.

reconsider.name: Miami Museum Mile Passport
reconsider.reason: Overlaps with existing museum-ticket reward category (Fever); small regional scope adds little differentiation.
reconsider.why_fits: A city-run multi-venue passport program offering tradeable stamp-based rewards across five Miami attractions, filling a 'city pass / local attraction' gap distinct from NOMO's existing single-venue museum/concert partners. Families can collect museum stamps for local perks, with rewards available after three visits and a museum membership raffle for those who complete the full passport.

reconsider.name: Verizon Innovative Learning (Verizon)
reconsider.reason: Redundant with Verizon's Digital Wellness Initiative (same company); weaker fit since it's about device/tech access rather than screen-time reduction.
reconsider.why_fits: <cite index="24-1,24-2">Verizon Innovative Learning, in partnership with Digital Promise, works side-by-side with schools and districts to provide students with internet-connected devices and enhance how teachers use technology, with 33 new schools joining for 2026-27, bringing the program's impact to 693 schools nationwide.</cite> Exactly matches NOMO's 'US Telcos & MVNOs' distribution vertical with an active, scaling school-district program to plug into.

reconsider.name: Aetna
reconsider.reason: Redundant with the stronger, higher-confidence UnitedHealthcare insurance candidate.
reconsider.why_fits: <cite index="39-11,39-12">Aetna announced 'Aetna Mental Health On Demand to provide real time access to care and ongoing support,' where members aged 13 and older have real-time access to a licensed clinician through chat, phone or video</cite>. As a major health insurer already building teen-focused digital wellness infrastructure, Aetna fits the Insurance distribution/direct GTM vertical and is not yet in NOMO's partner lineup.

reconsider.name: AYSO (American Youth Soccer Organization)
reconsider.reason: Generic youth-sports program expansion with no clear tie to screen-time reduction or digital wellness; vague why_fits.
reconsider.why_fits: AYSO PLAY! is actively launching new community partnerships (e.g., with the Greater Tampa Boys & Girls Club after-school program running 5 days/week) as of May 2026, demonstrating an open, relationship-driven partnership posture that fits the parent/coach-buyer, large-roster profile of the Youth Sports vertical NOMO has yet to activate.

rejected_today.why_fits: <cite index="7-1,7-3">Wyzly, the first learn-to-earn screen time solution, lets kids earn 'Golden Keys' that unlock apps and screen time by answering questions correctly</cite>, competing in the same gamified screen-time-reward category NOMO occupies, with potential school/parent-market overlap.

rejected_today.reason: Vague general teen wellness app without a concrete competing reward/challenge mechanic to compare against NOMO.

rejected_today.name: AppBlock (MobileSoft)

rejected_today.why_fits: An actively updated (Nov 11, 2026) app-blocking tool explicitly marketing to students for study-focused blocking and running social-accountability challenges like 'No Scroll November', fitting the app-block/gamified competitor criteria.

rejected_today.category: Screen-time reward app with brand-funded cash/gift-card payouts for teens
rejected_today.name: Dayo
rejected_today.reason: Duplicate of the already-surfaced Dayo (Dayo Deals) competitor candidate.
rejected_today.why_fits: Dayo is a rewards-based app that pays teens (via Venmo/PayPal/gift cards from Starbucks, Adidas, Amazon) for hitting screen-time goals, directly overlapping NOMO's reward-for-reduced-screen-time model and brand-partner mechanic; it is not yet in NOMO's tracked competitor list.

rejected_today.name: Foot Locker FLX Rewards
rejected_today.reason: Too similar to existing Nike/Vans sneaker and apparel rewards; no new reward category.
rejected_today.why_fits: <cite index="69-3,69-5">FLX Rewards gives members priority access to highly anticipated sneaker launches, exclusive sales, member-only events, and an upgraded birthday gift designed to unlock their inner sneakerhead</cite>. This gives NOMO a tradeable inventory of exclusive sneaker drops/experiences for a Gen Z audience, complementing but distinct from existing Nike/Vans merch rewards.

rejected_today.name: Tickets for Teens (Theatre Development Fund)

rejected_today.why_fits: TDF's Tickets for Teens program gives members free admission to numerous NYC museums, zoos, gardens and cultural institutions on a rotating basis, filling the 'museum ticket / city pass' reward-inventory gap more deeply than NOMO's current Fever listing, with a teen-specific membership card model ready-made for integration.

rejected_today.why_fits: Already proven as a teen screen-time reward redemption brand (via competitor Dayo's gift-card payouts), Starbucks has tradeable, teen-familiar reward inventory comparable to NOMO's existing McDonald's ice-cream-cone partnership.

rejected_today.name: Adidas
rejected_today.reason: Redundant with existing Nike/Vans apparel rewards and only weakly sourced via a competitor's practice.
rejected_today.why_fits: Currently redeemable as a gift-card reward in a direct competitor's (Dayo) teen screen-time program, confirming Gen Z appeal and willingness to fund screen-time-reduction incentive programs — a natural complement to NOMO's existing Nike/Vans apparel partners.

rejected_today.name: Chipotle

rejected_today.why_fits: Pioneered a play-to-earn mechanic letting Gen Z users earn and redeem real-world food rewards for in-platform engagement, demonstrating an appetite for exactly the kind of 'free food for behavior' tradeable-reward partnership NOMO already runs with McDonald's.

rejected_today.name: TDF Tickets for Teens (NYC)

rejected_today.why_fits: A city-backed program offering NYC high schoolers free/low-cost Broadway, Off-Broadway, and museum access via a digital membership card — exactly the tradeable, teen-friendly reward inventory (museum tickets, city-style passes) NOMO's rewards lineup is built around, and not yet in its partner roster.

rejected_today.name: Dallas Teen All Access Pass
rejected_today.reason: A municipal benefit program, not a signable brand reward partner; overlaps with existing GetYourGuide/Fever categories.
rejected_today.why_fits: A municipal program giving Dallas teens free admission to museums, the zoo, library, Arboretum, and other city venues — a close match to the 'museum tickets, city green passes' reward criteria and a replicable model NOMO could pursue city-by-city alongside its municipality GTM vertical.

rejected_today.name: Go City (CityPASS-style multi-attraction pass)
rejected_today.reason: Duplicate of the Go City/CityPASS candidate; overlaps with existing Fever/GetYourGuide experience inventory.
rejected_today.why_fits: Go City is the world's largest multi-attraction city pass provider, offering bundled museum, tour, and activity tickets across dozens of cities — a direct match for NOMO's 'museum tickets, city green passes' reward category and complementary to existing partners like Fever and GetYourGuide without overlapping them. It is described as "a British travel company that offers discounted ticket packages to top tourist locations in 31 cities," with "over 7.5 million active users" and recognized as "the world's largest provider of tourist passes," giving NOMO access to large, tradeable reward inventory across many cities in one partnership.
